title: Comprehensive Evaluation of the Effectiveness and Safety of Placenta-Targeted Drug Delivery Using Three Complementary Methods
protocol: Synthesize MTX- and ICG-loaded lipid-polymer nanoparticles (MNPs and INPs respectively) as described elsewhere.
Synthesize plCSA-BP-conjugated nanoparticles (plCSA-MNPs and plCSA-INPs).
Place female CD-1 mice with a fertile male in one cage to observe vaginal plugs the following morning.
Define the mouse as embryonic day 0.5 (E0.5) if a vaginal plug is observed.
House pregnant mice alone in a pathogen-free animal room until E14.5.
Weigh the pregnant mouse at E11.5 to determine the quantity and volume of nanoparticle injection.
Sterilize nanoparticles by filtration through a 0.22 μm syringe filter before injection.
Warm the tail for 5-10 min with a heating pad to dilate the tail vein.
Inject nanoparticles into the pregnant mouse's tail vein.
Aspirate INPs or plCSA-INPs into a 28 g insulin syringe.
Transfer the pregnant mouse to a holding device that restrains the mouse while allowing access to the tail vein.
Clean the tail with an alcohol swab.
Insert the syringe into the tail vein.
Slowly inject the INPs or plCSA-INPs (5 mg/kg ICG equivalent) with even pressure over 5-10 s.
Stop injecting if a blister appears on the tail.
Apply gentle pressure to the injection site until bleeding stops, which normally takes 30-60 s.
Image the pregnant mice using the in vivo fluorescence imaging system 30 min after injection.
Anesthetize the pregnant mice with an oxygen flow rate of 1.0 L/min and isoflurane at 2-4% in an associated chamber of the anesthesia unit.
Verify full anesthesia by slow and regular breathing.
Place a nose cone over the mouth and nose to allow inhalation of 1-2% isoflurane with an oxygen flow rate of 1.0 L/min to maintain anesthesia.
Move the mice into the imaging chamber, keeping them in a supine position.
Select 2D-fluorescence and photographic parameters to image ICG fluorescence signals.
Set exposure to auto and excitation/emission wavelengths to 710/820 nm.
Turn off isoflurane influx at the end of imaging procedure.
Return pregnant mice carefully to their cages.
Anesthetize pregnant mice with isofluorane 48 hours after nanoparticle injection.
Sacrifice dam by cervical dislocation.
Collect fetuses and placentas using Graefe forceps, tissue forceps, and dissecting scissors.
Place placentas and fetuses into the imaging chamber.
Image using method described in step 2.3.4.
Obtain and prepare pregnant mice as described in step 2.1.
Use HFUS to image pregnant mice at E6.5.
Confirm pregnancy by visualizing embryos on day E6.5.
Randomly allocate pregnant mice into three groups: MNP group, plCSA-MNP group, PBS group.
Inject PBS, MNPs or plCSA-MNPs (1 mg/kg MTX equivalent) into tail veins of pregnant mice every other day starting at E6.5.
Image pregnant mice using HFUS imaging system 24 hours after nanoparticle injection.
Anesthetize the pregnant mice as described in step 2.3.2.
Turn on the integrated temperature controls of the imaging platform and preheat to 37-42 °C.
Secure the pregnant mice in a supine position using tape.
Place the nose cone connected to the anesthesia unit over the snout.
Apply 2% isoflurane with an oxygen flow rate of 1.0 L/min to maintain steady anesthesia.
Remove hair from the abdomen using a depilatory cream.
Wipe out residual depilatory cream thoroughly with water-soaked gauze.
Coat the abdomen with acoustic coupling gel.
Place the 40 MHz transducer in the mechanical arm.
Adjust the transducer position to obtain longitudinal images of the fetus and placenta.
Click the B-Mode button and lower the transducer over the abdomen until the fetus and placenta come into view.
Press Scan/Freeze to initiate or stop imaging.
Press Cine store to store cine loop images.
Press Frame store to store frame images.

Click the Measure button to analyze gestational sac length (GS), fetal crown rump length (CRL), biparietal diameter (BPD), abdominal circumference (AC), placental diameter (PD) and placental thickness (PT).
Click the PW button and place the sampling volume box in the center of the umbilical artery.
Press Scan/Freeze to initiate imaging and Cine store to collect umbilical artery images.
Click Measure to calculate the umbilical artery peak velocity (UA).
Click the Color button and adjust the transducer position to obtain fetal heart images.
Press Scan/freeze to initiate imaging and Cine store to collect fetal heart images.
Click Measure to calculate the fetal heart rate (HR).
Inject pregnant mice with a single dose of MNPs or plCSA-MNPs at late pregnancy.
Anesthetize the mice by an intraperitoneal injection of avertin.
Verify full anesthesia in the mice by checking for response to a foot pinch.
Spray the chest area with 75% ethanol.
Perform cardiac perfusion through the left ventricle with ice-cold 0.9% saline.
Euthanize the dam after perfusion.
Collect fetuses and placentas via cesarean section using forceps and scissors.
Store collected tissues at -80°C prior to analysis.
Prepare the homogenization solution (10% perchloric acid) and keep on ice.
Collect approximately 200 mg of tissue, and add 500 μl of homogenization solution to each sample.
Homogenize the samples using a homogenizer at full speed for 30 s.
Repeat the homogenizing procedure twice.
Centrifuge the samples at 14,000 ×g for 20 min at 4°C.
Filter the supernatant (approximately 300 μl) through a 0.45 μm syringe filter.
Transfer the resulting liquid to an HPLC vial.
Place sample vials into an autosampler tray for injection.
Prepare the mobile phase solution: 40 mM potassium phosphate dibasic (pH 4.5) and acetonitrile (88:12, v/v).
Filter the mobile phase solution through a 0.45 μm pore size syringe filter.
Transfer the resulting liquid to a clean HPLC reservoir bottle.
Adjust the pH with 0.1 M phosphoric acid if necessary.
Use ultrasonic vibration for 15 min to degas the mobile phase prior to use each time.
Weigh 10 mg of MTX into a 1.5 ml centrifuge tube.
Add 1 ml of 1 M sodium hydroxide to dissolve the MTX completely.
Vortex at high speed until the MTX dissolves completely.
Dilute 50 μl of the primary stock in 950 μl of the mobile phase to create a secondary MTX stock (500 μg/ml).
Store the secondary MTX stock on ice until use.
Make further dilutions to create the standards as specified in Table 1.
Store the prepared standards on ice and prepare them fresh daily.
Run the standards alongside the experimental samples in series.
Turn on the HPLC degasser to remove air from the system.
Turn on the flow, equilibrating the column with the mobile phase for 7.5 hours (30 min) to reduce baseline noise.
Set the temperature of the column to 25 °C.
Inject 20 μL sample volumes at a flow rate of 1 mL/min.
Click the Run Method button to start the analysis.
Manually change the mobile phase to HPLC-grade acetonitrile when runs are complete.
Run for approximately 15 min to protect the system.
Calculate the areas under the standard MTX peaks using the HPLC system software.
